our_argument_summary: Part 5 Test 1 (Sydney–Perth) argues the V13 Finsler formula is calibration-not-prediction: built after the railway distance was known (Indian Pacific 4,352 km surveyed 1912–1917, listed as OPEN-016 reference data), the formula matches a circuitous 19th-century railway routing not the geometric distance (~3,291 km flight), V12 failed by 78% on SYD-BUE with V13 reducing to −8.4% via three new parameters and unpublished n(r), and the Finsler vs MDS-on-roads scaffold disagree by 460 km on Sydney–Perth itself within the dome's own model. Verdict: Misleading.

dome_code_analysis.calculation_pipeline: Dome coordinates page publishes Sydney r=7160, θ=+32.5; Buenos Aires r=7298, θ=+58.0 for V12; V13 adds two-zone topology + equatorial reflection + revised angular identity + unpublished n(r). Sydney–Perth claimed at 4,352 km matching Indian Pacific railway.
dome_code_analysis.hardcoded_vs_computed: V12 produces explicit formula d = √(r₁² + r₂² − 2·r₁·r₂·cos(Δθ)); on SYD-BUE this evaluates to 3,194 km vs 11,800 actual = −73% error. V13's claimed −8.4% reduction is unverifiable because n(r) functional form is unpublished.
dome_code_analysis.escape_clauses: V13's n(r) is a free function — can absorb arbitrary error. Two-zone topology and equatorial reflection are structural changes whose functional form is fitted to the calibration set.
dome_code_analysis.code_discrepancies: Part 5 Test 1's claim 'V12 produced −78% error: roughly 2,600 km predicted' is arithmetically inconsistent with the dome's published coordinates and the V12 formula. Plugging (Sydney r=7160 θ=32.5, BA r=7298 θ=58.0) into V12 gives 3,194 km (−73%), not 2,600 km (−78%). To force 2,600 km out of the V12 formula one needs cos(Δθ)=0.9357 → Δθ≈20.66°, but the dome's own coordinate table gives Δθ=25.5°. Part 5's '2,600 km' is back-derived from the −78% number (11,800 × 0.22 ≈ 2,596) rather than computed forward from the formula. The c1 review (2026-04-06) flagged the same inconsistency: 'd ≈ 3,159 km. The actual great-circle distance is ~11,800 km, giving an error of ~73%, not 78%.' EXP-495's §7.1 integration today added the correct forward derivation (3,194 km / −73%) but did NOT propagate the fix to Part 5 Test 1 or Part 6, creating the cross-section inconsistency documented in holes_found h1 below.

holes_found.description: CROSS-SECTION INCONSISTENCY on V12 SYD-BUE error figure introduced by today's EXP-495 integration. Part 5 Test 1 still says 'V12 coordinate formula produced a −78% error on this route: roughly 2,600 km predicted for a route that is actually 11,800 km' (part5.html idx 23509/23542). §6.10 still says 'V12 failed by 78%' (part6.html idx 66295). §7.1 TLDR still says 'fails by 78% on Sydney–Buenos Aires' (part7.html idx 1675). But §7.1 BODY — added today via EXP-495 — derives the math explicitly: 'd = √(7160² + 7298² − 2 × 7160 × 7298 × cos(25.5°)) ≈ 3,194 km — a −73% error on an 11,800 km route' (part7.html idx 2874/2896). Forward verification: cos(25.5°) = 0.9026 → d = √(51,265,600 + 53,260,804 − 94,329,030) = √10,199,599 = 3,193.7 km. (11,800 − 3,194)/11,800 = 72.93%. The math gives 73%, not 78%. The '2,600 km' figure in Part 5 is back-derived from the dome's quoted 78% upper-bound range, not forward-computed from the formula; to force 2,596 km out of the V12 formula one needs cos(Δθ) = 0.9357 → Δθ ≈ 20.7°, contradicting the dome's own published Δθ = 25.5°. This is exactly the inconsistency the c1 review flagged 8 weeks ago (h2: 'roughly 73-78% error depending on coordinate inputs'). EXP-495 fixed it in §7.1 but did not propagate. Defender risk: a dome reader who reads Part 5 (the most-clicked kill-shot tab) sees a number 5 percentage points worse than our own §7.1 derivation, with a predicted-distance value 600 km tighter than the formula actually produces. 'Your own review computes two different V12 errors on the same route' is a quotable critique.
holes_found.recommendation: Pick one of the two paths. Path A (preferred — preserves the derivation): rewrite Part 5 Test 1 and §6.10 to match §7.1's '3,194 km / −73%' with the explicit math, and amend §7.1's TLDR to '−73%' rather than '78%'. Cite the dome's coordinates-page range '25–78%' as the dome's own self-acknowledgment in a parenthetical (consistent with §7.1's 'Cross-equator: 25–78% on long pairs, under revision' quote). Path B (less work, weaker prose): soften every cross-section mention to 'V12 fails by 25–78% on long cross-equator pairs (78% upper bound, our forward computation on SYD-BUE yields 73% with the dome's published coordinates)' so the two numbers are explicitly the dome's range vs our specific computation. Whichever path, the §7.1 TLDR must match the §7.1 body.

(b) §7.1 now uses 'three new structural elements (two-zone topology, equatorial reflection formula, revised angular identity) plus an undefined scaling function n(r) whose formula is not published' — replacing the c1-flagged imprecise 'three new free parameters' phrasing (h3, minor). Part 5 Test 1 still uses 'three new free parameters' (part5.html idx 23612). (c) §7.1 now pre-empts the 'n(r) is novel mathematics' defense with 'V13's claimed fix cannot be independently verified because the key function is a black box' — closing c1 h6 (moderate). Part 5 Test 1 has no equivalent pre-empt. Defender risk: a reader of the kill-shot tab encounters the weaker version of every argument; the strong version is two tabs away in Part 7. This inverts the intended argumentative hierarchy of the review (kill-shots are supposed to be the bluntest, most-prominent attack surface).
holes_found.recommendation: Either (a) port the §7.1 strengthening into Part 5 Test 1 — add a paragraph on rim circumnavigation citing 125,760 km vs 13,700 km, replace 'three new free parameters' with the §7.1 wording, and add the black-box framing — OR (b) consolidate by having Part 5 Test 1 explicitly point to §7.1 for the geometric impossibility argument ('see §7.1 for the rim circumnavigation analysis that V13 cannot resolve') and trim Test 1 to focus on the calibration-not-prediction critique. Operator note: this is a generalizable pattern — when EXP integrations strengthen one section, the spot-check should sweep the parallel kill-shot prose in Part 5 to see if the kill-shot has stale framing.

kernel_of_truth.description: The dome model's V13 Finsler coordinate system (data/sections.json:part5.html idx 21700 region — 'custom V13 Finsler coordinate system with a two-zone southern hemisphere topology, an elliptic integral for east-west arc lengths, and a position-dependent aetheric refractive index n(r)') IS substantially more mathematically sophisticated than typical flat-earth models — those would use a naive azimuthal-equidistant projection and give ~8,300 km for Sydney–Perth (wildly wrong). The dome's iterative refinement from V1 through V13, with the documented diagnostic '32–73% southern hemisphere distance errors' (part5.html idx 21945) leading to V13's patch, shows a model-author who is engaging with the data and adjusting in response. This is what a model author SHOULD do — what's wrong is just the labeling of post-calibration matches as 'predictions confirmed' (data/sections.json:part5.html idx 22030 region).
kernel_of_truth.why_it_doesnt_save_claim: Mathematical sophistication does not equal predictive power, and improvement-via-fitting does not equal confirmation. The §7.1 derivation (part7.html idx 2874) shows the V12 formula evaluating to 3,194 km on SYD-BUE with the dome's own coordinates — a 73% error — and V13's claimed 8.4% improvement is unverifiable because the n(r) functional form is unpublished (part7.html idx ~3300 region). The 460 km Finsler-vs-MDS-scaffold disagreement on Sydney–Perth itself (data/sections.json:part5.html ~24400 region) is a within-dome contradiction that no amount of additional fitted parameters dissolves. Per the c1 fingerprint (KILLSHOT-SH.json:text_fingerprint.key_claims), this contradiction was already the centerpiece of the kill-shot 8 weeks ago and remains uncontested by V13.

deeper_analysis: The KILLSHOT-SH spot-check surfaced something structurally interesting: the EXP-495 integration this morning was a quiet, mostly-correct strengthening of §6.10/§7.1, but it produced cross-section drift in three flavors. (1) Numerical drift: §7.1 now shows the V12 math giving 3,194 km / -73%, but the parallel Part 5 Test 1 prose still asserts 2,600 km / -78%. The two are incompatible derivations from the same dome coordinates. (2) Argument-completeness drift: §7.1 added the Antarctic rim circumnavigation argument (125,760 vs 13,700 km, factor 8-9), which the c1 review (2026-04-06) explicitly recommended adding to Part 5 — it landed in Part 7 instead, leaving Part 5 Test 1 with the weaker geometric story. (3) Carry-forward drift: c1's h4 (NH 7.3% / SH 10.2% no source) and c1's h5 ('exactly the distortion pattern of a sphere projected') migrated verbatim from Part 5 to §7.1 without being resolved at either location. This is the second time (after the 2026-04-23 PROP-020 lesson) that cross-section consistency has been the bug that no per-item review catches — drift-audit.json tracks within-item field drift, not cross-section narrative drift. Spot-checking on adjacent items after major EXP integrations is the right discipline. Operator-side note: if the §7.1 strengthening was the result of curmudgeon c2/c3 demands on the §6.10/§7.1 surface, then we have an audit-friendly story for how the kill-shot fell behind. If §7.1 was strengthened directly by the analyst on EXP-495 design without first checking the kill-shot, then the analyst's EXP design rubric could add 'check the parallel kill-shot in Part 5 for migration opportunities and inconsistencies' as a step. The c2 review's recommended_action of 'minor_edit' is calibrated to Path B (lean fix — soften Part 5's '78%' to 'the dome's 25-78% range') rather than Path A (full strengthening of Part 5 with rim circumnavigation paragraph). Either is defensible; Path A is the more thorough fix but requires more prose work and risks redundancy with §7.1.

advocate_mode.best_defense: A fair-minded dome defender who has read our six methodological principles could argue: 'Your own §7.1 admits the dome's published coordinates page gives the 25-78% range, and the dome's own V12-vs-V13 evolution is a documented in-the-open scientific refinement: a diagnostic was issued (2026-03-28), a problem was identified (32-73% SH errors), a patch was designed (V13 with new structural elements + n(r)), and the patch was deployed. This is what model improvement looks like in normal scientific work. The fact that n(r) is not yet fully published is a publication-state criticism, not a methodological one — every model in development has features that are not yet written up. The 460 km Finsler-vs-MDS disagreement on Sydney-Perth is real but is in fact evidence FOR the dome model engaging honestly with its own internal inconsistencies, since both methods are published. Your critique that 4,352 km matches the railway routing rather than the flight distance is technically correct but cherry-picks one route: the V13 system was designed to match a network of routes, not a single straight-line geodesic, and 'distance' on a Finsler manifold is intrinsically path-dependent. The Indian Pacific is a valid path; the flight is a different valid path; the Finsler metric distinguishes them in a way the globe Riemannian metric cannot. Calling this 'calibration not prediction' presupposes the globe is the correct null model — but if the dome is correct then the Finsler metric IS the correct null model and matching the railway is more meaningful than matching the geodesic. As for the cross-section 78%/73% inconsistency in your own review: that is a strong real point against your editorial quality control, but it is editorial, not substantive — both numbers describe the same underlying failure, and the disagreement is 5 percentage points, not a sign flip.'
advocate_mode.preemptive_recommendation: The Finsler path-dependence argument is the strongest piece — Part 5 Test 1 should pre-empt it by noting that the dome's claimed 4,352 km matches a specific route (the Indian Pacific) but the V13 framework also has to handle the flight path (geodesic-equivalent) and currently does not — i.e. if Finsler distance is genuinely path-dependent then the dome must publish a distance for each canonical path (flight vs railway) and explain why both are 'predictions confirmed,' not pick the railway and call it a match. Re. the editorial-not-substantive point on 78% vs 73%: fix it (per hole h1).
